purpose: Fictional work scenarios with explicit facts and checkable reasoning; no private chat content

messages.content: An order has 4 items at $125 each. Shipping is $40. Tax is 10% of the item subtotal only; shipping is not taxed. The approved budget is $600. What is the final charge, and how much budget remains?

red_flags: Gives $594 or $600 as the final charge

messages.content: A support ticket arrives Monday at 16:20. The deadline is 2 business hours after arrival. Business hours are 09:00–17:00 Monday through Friday, with no holidays and no breaks. What day and time is the deadline?

review: Counts 40 business minutes on Monday and 80 on Tuesday

messages.content: These are attempt log rows, not distinct requests: (r1, 09:00, timeout), (r1, 09:02, success), (r2, 09:03, success), (r3, 09:04, timeout). Each ID is one request; later attempts replace earlier outcomes for that ID. How many attempts are logged, how many unique requests are there, and how many unique requests ended in success?

review: Two unique requests ended in success: r1 and r2
red_flags: Treats r1 as a final timeout
Counts two attempts for r1 as two successful requests

cases.area: inventory with reservations and inbound stock

messages.content: A warehouse has 12 units physically on hand, of which 5 are reserved. Four more units are due tomorrow but have not arrived. Today it ships 3 unreserved units. Immediately after shipping, how many units are physically on hand and how many are available for new orders? Do not count tomorrow's delivery.

review: Four units available: nine on hand minus five reserved
red_flags: Counts the inbound four as on hand
Ships reserved stock despite the stated unreserved shipment

messages.content: Task A takes 3 hours and task B takes 2 hours. Different workers can start A and B at the same time. Task C takes 1 hour and cannot start until both A and B finish. There is no other delay. Starting at 09:00, what is the earliest completion time? Explain which task controls it.

review: A controls the wait: A ends 12:00, B ends 11:00, then C ends 13:00
red_flags: Starts C when B finishes at 11:00

messages.content: The rule says a release may ship only when tests pass AND the owner approves. Tests passed. The approval status was not provided. Can you conclude the release may ship? Can you conclude it may not ship? Give the precise conclusion from the available facts.

review: Cannot conclude it may not ship

messages.content: A service received 70 distinct requests. Sixty returned a usable answer, five timed out, and five returned a client error. What percentage of all requests returned a usable answer? What percentage of requests that did not return a client error returned a usable answer? Give both fractions and percentages to one decimal place.

red_flags: Uses 65 as the denominator for both

cases.area: snapshots do not reveal intermediate value

messages.content: A counter snapshot at 14:00 reads 100. Another snapshot at 14:05 reads 95. No events between the snapshots were recorded, and the counter can move up or down. What exactly did it read at 14:03? If this cannot be determined, say so and explain why a straight-line estimate is not evidence.

review: Says the exact 14:03 value cannot be determined
Explains endpoints alone do not establish the path between them
red_flags: Assumes a straight-line change without evidence

cases.area: corrected instruction and source of truth

messages.content: For a rollout, send the draft to QA before sending it to the owner.
I will send it to the owner first, then QA.
My earlier instruction was reversed in your reply. The updated plan is: send it to Legal first, then QA, then the owner. Which recipient is first, second, and third?

review: Legal first, QA second, owner third
Follows the latest user instruction rather than the assistant's earlier reversal

messages.content: A small ledger has four events: payment A received $50; payment B received $80; refund against payment A sent $20; payment C attempted $90 but failed and no money moved. What is the net cash received from these events? List which events affect cash.

review: Includes $50 and $80 receipts, subtracts $20 refund, excludes failed $90 attempt
red_flags: Counts the failed payment as cash
